AurelianPracticePage1.label: What We Do

items.title: Dispute Resolution
items.subtitle: Litigation & Arbitration
items.excerpt: Litigation, arbitration and mediation - from first advice to final appeal.

image.alt: Wooden judge's gavel on a dark desk

overview: Disputes are costly, stressful and distracting. Our dispute resolution team helps you choose the right forum - negotiation, mediation, arbitration or court - and builds a strategy around your commercial goals.
We represent clients in contract, property, shareholder, construction and professional negligence disputes, and enforce judgments and arbitral awards at home and abroad.

faqs.question: Should I go to court or arbitration?
faqs.answer: It depends on your contract, the value in dispute, confidentiality needs and how quickly you need a result. We assess all options in the first consultation.

faqs.question: How long does a typical dispute take?
faqs.answer: Many disputes settle within three to six months. Contested court cases can take one to three years; we give you a realistic timeline from the outset.

faqs.question: Can you help enforce a judgment I already have?
faqs.answer: Yes. We trace assets and use every available enforcement route, including against parties located overseas.

tileImage.alt: Wooden judge's gavel on a dark desk

items.title: Criminal Defence
items.subtitle: Conventional & Economic Offences
items.excerpt: Robust defence from investigation to trial.

image.alt: Police patrol car parked on a city street

overview: A criminal allegation can threaten your liberty, career and reputation. Our defence lawyers act immediately - from the police station to trial - to protect your rights at every stage.
We defend conventional offences as well as complex white-collar and economic offences, including fraud, bribery, money laundering and regulatory breaches.

faqs.question: What should I do if I am contacted by the police?
faqs.answer: Stay calm, say nothing beyond your identity, and call a lawyer immediately. We can attend interviews with you at short notice.

faqs.question: Is my conversation with you confidential?
faqs.answer: Yes. Everything you tell us is protected by attorney-client privilege.

faqs.question: Do you defend companies as well as individuals?
faqs.answer: Yes. We advise companies and their directors on internal investigations and regulatory prosecutions.

tileImage.alt: Police patrol car parked on a city street

items.title: Corporate & Contracts
items.subtitle: Contracting & Transaction Law
items.excerpt: Contracts and deals that protect your business.

image.alt: Business person signing a contract

overview: Well-drafted contracts prevent disputes before they start. We draft, review and negotiate agreements that reflect the deal you actually made and protect you if things go wrong.
Our corporate team also advises on mergers, acquisitions, joint ventures, shareholder arrangements and corporate governance.

faqs.question: Can you review a contract someone has sent me?
faqs.answer: Yes. We usually return a marked-up draft with a short risk summary within two to three business days.

faqs.question: Do you offer fixed fees for contracts?
faqs.answer: For most standard agreements we offer a fixed fee agreed in advance.

faqs.question: Do you handle cross-border transactions?
faqs.answer: Yes, working with trusted partner firms in other jurisdictions where local law applies.

items.title: Insolvency & Bankruptcy
items.subtitle: Restructuring & Recovery

image.alt: Financial statements and a calculator on a desk

overview: Financial distress calls for fast, clear decisions. We advise companies and directors on restructuring options and help creditors recover what they are owed.
Our team acts in insolvency proceedings, debt recovery claims and director liability matters, always looking for the solution that preserves the most value.

faqs.question: My company is struggling - what are my duties as a director?
faqs.answer: Once insolvency is likely, your duties shift towards creditors. Early advice protects both the business and you personally.

faqs.question: How can I recover an unpaid debt?
faqs.answer: We start with a formal demand and, if needed, move to court or insolvency proceedings to enforce payment.

faqs.question: Is restructuring better than liquidation?
faqs.answer: Often yes, if the business is viable. We model both options so you can decide with full information.

tileImage.alt: Financial statements and a calculator on a desk

items.title: Employment & Labour Law
items.subtitle: Employers & Employees
items.excerpt: Workplace advice for employers and employees.

image.alt: Two colleagues discussing work at a laptop

overview: Employment relationships are governed by fast-changing laws. We help employers build compliant policies and help employees enforce their rights.
From contracts and handbooks to discrimination claims and senior executive exits, we resolve workplace issues quickly and discreetly.

faqs.question: I think I was wrongfully dismissed. What can I do?
faqs.answer: Strict time limits apply, so contact us quickly. We will review your contract and the circumstances and explain your options.

faqs.question: Can you audit our HR policies?
faqs.answer: Yes. We review contracts, handbooks and procedures and provide a prioritised action list.

faqs.question: Do you represent employees as well as employers?
faqs.answer: Yes, subject to conflict checks, we act for both.

tileImage.alt: Two colleagues discussing work at a laptop

items.title: Intellectual Property
items.subtitle: Trademark, Copyright & Data
items.excerpt: Protect your brand, ideas and data.

image.alt: Hands typing on a laptop keyboard

overview: Your ideas and brand are often your most valuable assets. We help you register, license and defend trademarks, copyrights, patents and trade secrets.
We also advise technology companies on IT contracts, data protection and privacy compliance.

faqs.question: How long does trademark registration take?
faqs.answer: Typically eight to twelve months if there are no objections. We run a clearance search first to reduce the risk.

faqs.question: Someone is copying my product. What can I do?
faqs.answer: We send a cease-and-desist letter and, if needed, seek an injunction and damages.

faqs.question: Do I need a privacy policy?
faqs.answer: If you collect any personal data online, almost certainly yes. We draft policies that match how you actually use data.

tileImage.alt: Hands typing on a laptop keyboard

items.title: Immigration Law
items.subtitle: Visas & Business Establishment

image.alt: Passenger aeroplane taking off

overview: Immigration processes are detailed and unforgiving of mistakes. We prepare complete, well-evidenced applications that give you the best chance of success first time.
We also advise overseas companies on establishing a presence and relocating key staff.

faqs.question: Which visa is right for me?
faqs.answer: It depends on your purpose, qualifications and plans. We assess your profile and recommend the most suitable route.

faqs.question: My application was refused. Can you help?
faqs.answer: Yes. We review the refusal and advise whether to appeal, request a review or reapply.

faqs.question: Can you help my company hire overseas staff?
faqs.answer: Yes. We handle sponsorship, compliance and individual applications for your employees.

items.title: Family & Private Client
items.subtitle: Families, Wills & Estates

image.alt: A family holding hands on a beach at sunset

overview: Family matters are personal. We combine legal skill with empathy to help you through separation, custody arrangements and financial settlements.
Our private client lawyers also help you plan ahead with wills, trusts and estate administration, protecting your family's future.

faqs.question: Do we have to go to court to divorce?
faqs.answer: Not always. Many couples reach agreement through negotiation or mediation, which is faster and less stressful.

faqs.question: When should I make a will?
faqs.answer: As soon as you have assets or dependants - and review it after any major life event.

faqs.question: Is our first meeting confidential?
faqs.answer: Completely. Nothing you share is disclosed without your consent.

tileImage.alt: A family holding hands on a beach at sunset

items.title: Start-up Advisory
items.subtitle: Founders & Emerging Companies

image.alt: Start-up team working together on laptops

overview: Getting the legal foundations right early saves founders time and money later. We help you incorporate, split equity fairly and protect your IP from day one.
As you grow, we support fundraising rounds, employee share plans and commercial contracts with flexible, start-up friendly fees.
services: Terms of service and privacy policies

faqs.question: Which company structure should I choose?
faqs.answer: It depends on your funding plans and where your founders are based. We explain the pros and cons of each structure.

faqs.question: Do you offer start-up packages?
faqs.answer: Yes. We offer fixed-fee launch packages and monthly retainers for early-stage companies.

faqs.question: Can you review a term sheet from an investor?
faqs.answer: Yes, usually within 48 hours, with a plain-English summary of the key terms.

items.title: Know Your Rights When You Are Arrested
items.author: Marcus Reed

image.alt: Statue of Lady Justice with scales

items.excerpt: An arrest is frightening. Knowing a few key rights can protect you from mistakes that are hard to undo later.

content.text: Being arrested is one of the most stressful experiences a person can face. In the moment, it is easy to say or do something that harms your defence later. Knowing your basic rights helps you stay calm and protected.
1. You have the right to remain silent
Apart from confirming your identity, you do not have to answer questions. Politely say that you wish to remain silent and want to speak to a lawyer.
2. You have the right to a lawyer
Ask for a lawyer immediately and do not discuss the case until one is present. A lawyer can attend interviews and advise you on bail.
The most important call you make after an arrest is to your lawyer - before you say anything else.
3. Do not consent to searches
Unless officers have a warrant or another lawful basis, you can decline consent to a search. Do not physically resist - simply state that you do not consent.

items: Write down everything as soon as you can

items.title: Preparing for Your First Court Hearing
items.author: Sophia Lane

image.alt: Wooden gavel and sound block on a white surface

items.excerpt: What to bring, what to wear and what to expect - a simple checklist for your first day in court.

content.text: Your first court hearing can feel intimidating, but good preparation makes a big difference to both your confidence and the outcome.
Before the hearing
Review your documents with your lawyer, confirm the time and courtroom, and plan to arrive at least 30 minutes early.
In the courtroom
Dress smartly, switch off your phone, stand when the judge enters and address the judge respectfully. Let your lawyer do the talking unless you are asked to speak.
Judges notice preparation and respect - both start long before you enter the courtroom.

items.title: Five Clauses Every Business Contract Needs
items.author: Olivia Hart

image.alt: Business documents and a laptop on a desk

items.excerpt: Many disputes start with a missing clause. These five provisions protect your business when things go wrong.

content.text: A contract is only as strong as its weakest clause. Here are five provisions we recommend in almost every commercial agreement.
1. Clear scope of work
Describe exactly what is being delivered, by when and to what standard. Vague scope is the number one cause of disputes.
2. Payment terms
Set out amounts, due dates, interest on late payment and what happens if payment is withheld.
3. Limitation of liability
Cap the amount each party can claim and exclude losses you cannot control.
The best time to agree how a dispute will be resolved is before the dispute exists.

items.title: When Should You Settle a Legal Dispute?
items.author: Sophia Lane

image.alt: Two business people shaking hands

items.excerpt: Settlement is not surrender. Here is how to weigh the costs, risks and benefits of resolving a dispute early.

content.text: Most legal disputes never reach a final judgment - they settle. Knowing when and how to settle can save you significant time, money and stress.
Weigh the real cost of going to trial
Consider legal fees, management time, reputational impact and the risk of losing. A good settlement often beats an uncertain win.
Use mediation
A neutral mediator can help both sides find common ground, often in a single day.
A fair settlement today is often worth more than a perfect judgment three years from now.

items.title: How Thorough Legal Research Wins Cases
items.author: Daniel Whitmore

image.alt: Warm-lit shelves of old law books

items.excerpt: Behind every winning argument is hours of careful research. Here is how we prepare - and why it matters to you.

content.text: Cases are rarely won by courtroom drama alone. They are won by preparation - and preparation starts with research.
Finding the right precedent
We review recent and historic decisions to find the authorities that support your position and anticipate the arguments of the other side.
Testing every argument
Before a hearing, we test each argument internally, so there are no surprises in court.
We never stop until we win - and winning starts at the library desk.

items.excerpt: Fair pay, safe conditions and protection from discrimination - a quick guide to your rights at work.

content.text: Every employee is entitled to certain basic protections. Understanding them helps you spot problems early and resolve them before they escalate.
Key rights to know

items: A written statement of your terms

content.text: What to do if your rights are breached
Keep records, raise the issue in writing and seek advice quickly - many claims have short time limits.
Good employers benefit from clear rules just as much as employees do.

items.title: An Estate Planning Checklist for Families
items.author: Emma Brooks

image.alt: Leather-bound books and a fountain pen

items.excerpt: A will is just the start. Use this checklist to make sure your family is fully protected.

content.text: Estate planning is not only for the wealthy. It is about making sure the people you love are cared for and your wishes are respected.
Your checklist

items: Consider a trust for complex assets

content.text: Review regularly
Marriage, divorce, children and property purchases all affect your plan. Review it every few years or after any major change.
Planning ahead is one of the kindest things you can do for your family.

items.title: Trademark Basics for Small Businesses
items.author: Grace Morgan

image.alt: Bookshelves filled with colourful books

items.excerpt: Your brand name is valuable. Here is how to check it, register it and stop others from copying it.

content.text: A strong brand takes years to build and can be copied overnight. Registering a trademark gives you the legal tools to protect it.
Search before you launch
A clearance search shows whether someone already owns a similar mark - saving you from an expensive rebrand later.
Register in the right classes
Trademarks are registered for specific goods and services. Choose classes that cover what you sell now and plan to sell soon.
Register early, monitor often and act quickly against copycats.
